title: Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility Services AE IDIQ, Unrestricted
description: THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED PROCUREMENT. This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for multi-discipline Architect-Engineer (A-E) services for Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility services at various Navy and Marine Corps installations primarily in the Navy Region Southwest but may also include work worldwide. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 USC Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR 36. The IDIQ contract will be for a base period of two (2) years and three (3) one-year option periods (if exercised). The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed $30,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term (including option years) is $1,000. Firm-fixed price task orders will be negotiated for this contract. The minimum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $25,000. The maximum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $2,500,000. There will be no dollar limit per year. Estimated start date is March 2027. The Small Business size standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330 (Engineering Services). The Government seeks the most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. Primary A-E Services: 1. Land Use Planning. 2. Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (AICUZ) and Range Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (RAICUZ) Studies. 3. Encroachment Action Plans (EAP) or Encroachment Control Plans (ECP). 4. Strategic Engagement and Communication Plans (SECP). 5. Outreach Planning Materials. 6. Electronic Database. Secondary Services: 1. Other related studies/analysis: Provide additional services to assist in implementation of encroachment management studies, Range Complex Management Plans (RCMP), Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMP), Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program plans, and other special planning, engineering, and encroachment support deliverables, such as analytical assessments, geospatial analysis and simulations, traffic studies, glint/glare analysis, radar assessments, plume analysis and modeling, lighting studies, and socio-economic studies. 2. Other Related Reports or Documentation: Deliverables also include assistance with incidental services related to providing public notice for studies and publicizing and providing training on encroachment-related studies. Please see attached synopsis for full synopsis description/instructions.

title: Sea Range Safety Surveillance Services
description: 1) INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE: NAWCWD is seeking technically competent sources for engineering services in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities related to Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Theater High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) programs at Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF). The purpose of this sources sought is to determine what companies are capable of providing the required services in a competitive procurement and to gain market knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications relative to the North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code 541330 for Engineering Services which has a corresponding size standard of $47 million. Responses to this sources sought synopsis will be utilized by the Government to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and make appropriate determinations about potential sources. No solicitation is currently available and as such this is not a request for proposal and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. A decision to set aside all or part of this requirement is dependent upon a review of the information submitted in response to this sources sought. After review of responses to this sources sought, a synopsis and/or solicitation announcement may be published. (2) PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This requirement is for engineering services to be provided in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities primarily related to Aegis-Based Defense, formerly Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Sea-Based Weapon Systems. Engineering service are provided to other entities, including (but not limited to) Program Executive Office Integrated Warfare Systems (PEO IWS), various Hypersonic programs, and Allied Foreign Military Sales (FMS) partners. Aegis-Based Defense is one weapon system in the layered defense provided for the United States and its deployed forces, friends and allies against ballistic missiles of all ranges in all phases of flight. This defense is provided through an integrated Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS), developed by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA). MDA is responsible for fulfilling the goals set out in the National Missile Defense Act of 1999 in deploying �as soon as is technologically possible an effective National Missile Defense system capable of defending the territory of the United States against limited ballistic missile attack�. In support of this goal, the Aegis-Based Defense program needs to collect high fidelity system under test and auxiliary sensor data in order to evaluate the results of the flight test and to determine if the system(s) met the mission objectives. Additionally, auxiliary sensor data is highly valuable in providing forensics for any anomalies that may have occurred during these events. Pre-/post-mission data analyses of this auxiliary sensor data is critical these flight test scenarios. This is a follow-on contract to N6893622D0024. The existing contract is Cost-Plus Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Level of Effort (LOE), and was awarded to Raytheon (RTX) on a sole source basis. The new contract will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP). (3) REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The MDA / Aegis-Based Defense program requires high fidelity pre-mission planning, real-time mission conduct and execution support, post-mission data analysis, and reporting of test results of high profile flight test events. Support shall be provided to various flight test events and systems engineering activities. This includes mission planning, test planning, generating test procedures, real-time mission conduct, data collection, real-time range safety mission support, mission data analyses and reporting, operations research support, and technical management support. Aegis-Based Defense requires support for test planning, test conduct, data reduction/analysis, and reporting of auxiliary sensor data during flight test events. This includes in-depth pre-mission analysis, which provides inputs to instrumentation, sensor data collection CONOPS, and sensor configurations to maximize valuable data collection. Recommendations for test support positions (TSPs) to auxiliary sensors will aid in maximizing valuable data collected. Inputs to test plans as well as mission requirements are needed to ensure mission test objectives are met. This includes auxiliary tracking and data collection objectives based on mission priorities and overall test objectives. Understanding test objectives will translate directly into what instrumentation should be used and how they should be configured. This includes inputs to all test participants (sea-based, ground-based, airborne, and space-based). Real-time mission conduct support assists auxiliary sensor participants to make adjustments to configurations, tracking objectives, and/or tracking CONOPS based on changes to mission scenarios. This support can ensure successful data collection during live missile and test vehicle launches. Mission conduct and execution support includes providing sensor and analysis support to assist range safety. Complex analyses and reporting of test results is needed to evaluate weapons and weapon systems to ensure mission test objectives have been met. This includes ingesting, reducing, processing, and analyzing all auxiliary data (optical, radar, telemetry) and data formats. Analyses and test results should be shared with the government and test community to ensure proper communication and collaboration. (4) PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: This effort will primarily be performed at PMRF at Barking Sands, Kauai, HI. Support will also be conducted at the following national test ranges and locations: Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH) on Oahu, HI; Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) Point Mugu Sear Range (PMSR) at Point Mugu, CA; Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB) in CA; Reagan Test Site (RTS) on Kwajalein Atoll; Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in AK; Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) at Cape Canaveral, FL; Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) at Patuxent River, MD; and the Missile Defense Integration and Operations Center (MDIOC) at Colorado Springs, CO. (5) CONTRACT TYPE: The Government is considering a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Idefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year Ordering Period. (6) SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The Government requests that responses to this sources sought include the following: demonstrated capability to ingest, reduce, process, and analyze auxiliary sensor data and applicable data formats for the MDA /Aegis-Based Defense program. Auxiliary sensor data includes optics, radar, and telemetry, and applicable formats include binary, ASCII, and movie formats (h264, mp4, mkv, avi, mpg, etc.). Data analyses includes data reduction, data tracking algorithms, signature generation, data display/visualization, brightness/contrast and image enhancement, data registration, image sequence output, and background subtraction. Demonstrated capability to generate an early track of a launch vehicle to provide a state vector solution to range safety entities for immediate awareness and assessment of the vehicle trajectory status to the range safety officer. This will allow range safety to take corrective action (if needed) and prevent the vehicle from violating range safety boundaries (i.e. � IIP destruct limits, safe firing bearings, etc.). This system must be capable of meeting all range safety assessment criteria, including latency times, data rate, and first state vector solution time. Demonstrate ability to support Navy optical data collection aircraft with optical Subject Matter Expert (SME) for mission planning, sensor calibrations, real-time inputs to tracking operators, mission conduct, and post-mission data analysis. Demonstrate familiarity with test ranges, range instrumentation, range safety criteria, and range data collection capabilities. Assessment of test range

description: The U.S. Coast Guard is looking for sources which would be interested in performing In Service Vehicle Sustainment (ISVS) and planned maintenance repairs for Coast Guard Cutter (CGC) HEALY. It is anticipated that requests for proposals would tentatively be issued around 2 April 2027 and the contract would be awarded around 15 October 2027. title: Market Intelligence for EIE483 and EIE484
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. NAICS Codes: EIE483 and EIE484 - 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Alaska District, has requirements for two separate Military Construction (MILCON) projects at Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska: EIE483 � Joint Mobility Center Expansion: Design and construct a new Deployment Processing Facility sited relative to the airfield and supporting facilities to be occupied by 354th Logistics Readiness Squadron personnel. The facility will contain areas for the Personnel Deployment Function, Cargo Deployment Function, and Deployment Control Center, plus building support spaces. The Personnel Deployment Function area will contain a non-sterile holding area for processing passengers, a manifesting office for weighing passengers with their gear, a sterile holding area for passengers who have been manifested and are awaiting mission briefing, and a second sterile holding area for mission briefings. The current schedule identifies design starting in FY27 and construction starting in FY29, with a period of performance from FY27 through FY31. EIE484 � 225-Bed Permanent Party Dormitory: Construct a 3-story permanent party dormitory to house 225 unaccompanied enlisted airmen. Construction will include slab-on-grade and steel frame with concrete masonry unit block veneer and insulated metal panel over metal studs at exterior walls. Supporting facilities include 200 parking spaces, extension of steam, water, and sewer utilities, power distribution, and land scaping to service the new facility. Main facility spaces include 225 dormitory units, activity space, communal kitchens, dorm management office, public restroom, laundry, theater/meeting space, elevator, and mechanical/utility space. The current schedule identifies design starting in FY27 and construction start in FY28, with a period of performance from FY27 through FY31. Estimated Acquisition Magnitudes: EIE483 � Joint Mobility Center Expansion: Approximately $249.2 million. EIE484 � 225-Bed Permanent Party Dormitory: Approximately $305 million. Planned Acquisition Strategy: The Government anticipates utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement for each project. The final delivery method has not been determined and may be Progressive Design-Build (PDB) or Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), as informed by market intelligence and Government requirements. The Alaska District is conducting market intelligence to assess industry capability and interest in supporting these efforts utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority permits the Secretary concerned, subject to applicable statutory requirements, to enter into transactions other than contracts, cooperative agreements, or grants for facility repair and construction projects, including planning, design, engineering, prototyping, piloting, and execution. This authority is distinct from the Department of Defense prototype OT authorities commonly associated with 10 U.S.C. � 4021 and 4022. The Government will use market-intelligence responses to inform the appropriate delivery method, acquisition approach, and project-specific terms for each requirement. The anticipated delivery approach is expected to include the following phases, subject to the final acquisition strategy and project-specific solicitation terms: Phase 1: Design and Pre-Construction Services. The OT Awardee shall collaborate with the Government and, as applicable, the Designer of Record (DOR) or project design team to support scope validation, constructability, cost estimating, schedule development, risk management, design coordination, and development of a proposed construction price. Phase 2: Final Design and Construction. Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design and completion of pre-construction activities, the Awardee may submit a proposed Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) or other agreed-upon construction price, as identified in the applicable solicitation. If the Government accepts the proposed price, the Government may authorize construction execution. If the parties cannot reach agreement on price or other required terms, the Government retains an off-ramp to complete the requirement through an alternative acquisition or delivery method. title: Germany – Lift installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Aufzüge
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Mandat: Entwicklung, Umsetzung und Einführung der Versorgungsregion Brugg (Alters- und Langzeitversorgung) – Pilotprojekt
description:
Der Regionalplanungsverband Brugg Regio lanciert zusammen mit dem Kanton Aargau ein Pilotprojekt zur Entwicklung, Umsetzung und Einführung einer Versorgungsregion Brugg im Bereich der Alters- und Langzeitversorgung. Ziel ist der Aufbau einer koordinierten, regional abgestimmten Versorgungsstruktur in Zusammenarbeit mit der bestehenden Koordinationsstelle Alter, den Gemeinden sowie weiteren lokalen Akteuren, gestützt auf das Konzept für die Pilotphase und die Gesundheitspolitische Gesamtplanung des Kantons Aargau.

Die Leistungserbringung wird als Mandat ausgeschrieben.

Das Pilotprojekt dauert 3 1/2 Jahre.


Zentrale Punkte in der Ausschreibung

A. Leistungsbeschreibung

  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung eines Versorgungskonzepts für eine künftige Versorgungsregion Brugg
  • Aufbau der Zusammenarbeit mit der bestehenden Koordinationsstelle Alter und den weiteren lokalen Akteuren
  • Erstellen einer Meilensteinplanung
  • Erarbeitung eines Wegweisers für die Bevölkerung zur Versorgungsregion
  • Entwickeln eines Monitorings zur Versorgungsregion
  • Entwicklung und Führung von statistischen Grundlagen und weiteren strategischen Aufgaben
  • Beratung der Gemeinden und Akteure der Versorgungsregion
  • Stakeholder-Management (Gemeinden, Leistungserbringer, Kanton)
  • Verfassen von Stellungnahmen zu politischen Vorstössen und Gesetzesvorlagen
  • Berichterstattung gegenüber der Arbeitsgruppe Gesundheit und dem Vorstand von Regio Brugg
  • Planung einer Verankerung der Versorgungsregion und deren Organisation nach der Pilotphase oder Abschluss des Projekts



B. Projektziele & Meilensteine

  • Jährliche Evaluation des Projektverlaufs an den Vorstand von Brugg Regio
  • Periodische mündliche Berichterstattung und Diskussion des Projektverlauf mit der Arbeitsgruppe Gesundheit (=Projektsteuerung) von Brugg Regio
  • Meilensteine gemäss Konzept zur Pilotphase
  • Abbruch- oder Anpassungsklauseln


C. Governance

  • Die Vergabe erfolgt durch den Vorstand Brugg Regio auf Antrag der Arbeitsgruppe.
  • Brugg Regio führt die Buchhaltung für das Pilotprojekt, Budgetverantwortung beim Mandatsträger und Arbeitsgruppe.
  • Die Projektbegleitung wird durch die Arbeitsgruppe wahrgenommen.
  • In der Arbeitsgruppe ist eine Vertretung der Verwaltung, welche den Zugang zur Verwaltung der beteiligten Gemeinden sicherstellt und beratend für Verwaltungsabläufe zur Verfügung steht.

title: Germany – Liability insurance services – Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung für die vorgezogene Schadstoffsanierung des Gasteig – Teil 4: Höherdeckung (Exzedent) Beteiligtenversicherer
description: Der Gasteig ist das große, zentral gelegene Kultur- und Bildungszentrum Münchens. Mit ca. 1,8 Millionen Besuchern und mehr als 1.800 Veranstaltungen pro Jahr ist er das größte Kulturzentrum Deutschlands. Nach einer über 30-jährigen, intensiven Nutzungsphase steht die Generalsanierung des Gebäudes an. Vorgelagert wird in den Jahren 2027-2028 die Schadstoffsanierung des Gebäudes erfolgen.Die Münchner Raumordnungsgesellschaft mbH (MRG) als Auftraggeberin (AG) beabsichtigt die bedarfsgerechte Versicherung während der vorgezogenen Schadstoffsanierung / des Rückbaus des Gasteigs im Rahmen einer Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung. Die Beschaffung der Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung erfolgt in vier Teilen.Der Führungsversicherer für die Grunddeckung der Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung wurde bereits ermittelt und beauftragt. In einem zweiten Verfahren folgte für die Grunddeckung die Ermittlung des/der Beteiligungsversicherer/s für die Grunddeckung. Dieses Verfahren steht kurz vor dem Abschluss.Der Vertrag für die Höherdeckung (Exzedent) wird in zwei weiteren Verfahren ausgeschrieben. Das Verfahren für den Führungsversicherer für die Höherdeckung wurde ebenfalls bereits gestartet.Gegenstand des vorliegenden Verfahrens ist die Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung für die vorgezogene Schadstoffsanierung – hier hinsichtlich des/der Beteiligtenversicherers für die Höherdeckung (Beschaffungsteil 4). In diesem Verfahren wird der im ersten Beschaffungsteil im Wege der Verhandlung ermittelte Vertrag zu Grunde gelegt; eine Verhandlung über Vertragsinhalte findet nicht statt. Es wird ein sog. Nicht offenes Verfahren gem. § 16 VgV durchgeführt. Dieses Verfahren wird jetzt gestartet. Die vorläufige Kontraktsumme beträgt 59 Mio. EUR.Der genaue Leistungsgegenstand ergibt sich aus den gesamten Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere der Police (Höherdeckung)– Vergabeunterlage D.01 nebst Anlagen sowie den Unterlagen zum Projekt – Vergabeunterlagen E_01.

description: Sønderborg Kommune, herefter benævnt ”Bygherre”, er i gang med en løbende udskiftning af den nuværende fossildrevne personbilflåde til elbiler. Derudover vedrører udbuddet alle nødvendige elarbejder mellem tilslutningspunktet og ladepunkterne, samt planlægning, projektering og udførelse af alle grave- og reetableringsarbejder, som er nødvendige for at etablere infrastrukturen. Det er for Bygherre vigtigt at indgå et samarbejde med en Operatør, som har forståelse for, at ladepunkterne er kritisk infrastruktur, da dele af den kommunale flåde er hjemmeplejebiler, som benyttes i en samfundsmæssig vigtig opgave. Sønderborg Kommune skal eje de indkøbte ladebokse og ladestandere mv. Derudover betaler Sønderborg Kommune tilslutningsafgifter og det løbende strømforbrug afregnes direkte med elselskabet. Disse betegnelser er synonymer i nærværende materiale, og betegner den vindende tilbudsgiver, samt dennes underentreprenører, der indgås kontrakt med. description: The competition is for three sub-contracts for framework agreements for transport services. The contracting authority has assessed the procurement against the Public Procurement Act § 5h and concluded that there is no requirement for apprentices in this procurement as the contract ́s main element does not include work where it is relevant to use labour with certificates of apprenticeship or craft, cf. the Procurement Act § 5h 2nd section letter c, subsidiary because the need requires specialised competence or for other reasons is not suitable for apprentices, Cf. the Public Procurement Act § 5h 4 paragraph. The following applies for sub-contract 1: The contracting authority has decided to set a minimum requirement from and including other contract years that vehicles used in the contract shall use biogas, hydrogen or electricity as an energy carrier. The requirement is meant to meet the Public Procurement Act §5b, which allows public contracting authorities to use climate and environmental requirements in the requirement specifications, if it is clear that this provides a better climate and environmental effect. The transport ́s direct emissions are obviously the most important part of the contract ́s total environmental impact. For example, a diesel vehicle with emissions of approx. 200 g CO₂/km and an annual driving length of 40,000 km will generate approx. 8 tonnes of CO₂ per annum. Hydrogen and battery electrical vehicles have zero direct emissions in the operational phase, while biogas vehicles in the lifetime perspective provide very low, and in some cases net negative, CO₂-equivalent emissions. The requirement gives a significant and substantiated reduction in total emissions over the contract ́s lifetime. The contracting authority has considered using climate and the environment only as the award criteria. Such a model would, however, only give a relative ranking between the tenders, without ensuring that the delivery is actually low- or zero-emission based. If prices or other criteria are weighted higher, fossil-based solutions can still win the competition. Furthermore, evaluating environmental performance involves methodology challenges connected to documentation, calculation assumptions (e.g. well-to-wheel vs. tank-to-wheel), inspections and verifiability, which can increase the risk of doubt. The minimum requirement reduces this risk by determining a clear and objective level for acceptable environmental performance. The requirement is justifiable, proportional and connected to the delivery. The market can deliver sufficient competition within the stipulated frameworks. The assessments listed above document the environmental, technical and legal considerations that form the basis for choosing requirements, and fulfil the contracting authority ́s justification obligation in accordance with the Public Procurement Act §5b.

title: Sweden – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Brief Contact Intervention (BCI) projekt
description: Institutionen för lärande, informatik, management och etik (LIME) bedriver forskning och utbildning som främjar praktisk implementering av forskningsrön och ny kunskap i folkhälsoarbete, vård och omsorg. Institutionen har två universitetsövergripande verksamhetsområden – pedagogisk utveckling och stödverksamhet samt forskning, utbildning och rådgivning på området hälso- och sjukvård- samt forskningsetik. Det är en spännande arbetsmiljö där forskning och utbildning står i fokus. BCI-tjänsten är en del av ett forskningsprojekt som bedrivs av Nationellt centrum för suicidforskning och prevention av psykisk ohälsa (NASP). NASP bistår regeringen och Region Stockholms beslutsfattare och invånare med kunskapsunderlag, kunskapsutveckling och kunskapsspridning. Vårt uppdrag är att genom forskning, strategiskt folkhälsoarbete, utbildning och informationsspridning bidra till att minska antalet självmord och självmordsförsök regionalt och nationellt. NASP bidrar även till att utveckla och stimulera kunskapsområdet självmord och självmordsprevention där utvärdering av olika interventioner utgör en viktig del. NASP söker en Leverantör, med erfarenhet av att kommunicera med suicidnära personer, för att utföra en Brief Contact Intervention (BCI) – en beprövad modell som i internationella studier visats sig kunna minska suicidala beteenden hos suicidnära personer. Med BCI avses här stödjande telefonsamtal till en person som har suicidtankar. Brief Contact Interventions (BCIs) är insatser där man på ett regelbundet och systematiskt sätt följer upp personer med förhöjd självmordsrisk via telefon, brev, sms eller liknande. BCI-insatser används främst som ett sätt att förmedla medmänskligt stöd och omtanke, samt till att uppmuntra till att söka hjälp vid behov eller behandlingsföljsamhet om sådan pågår. BCI-insatser är således inte någon terapeutisk behandling, och en fördel är att insatsen därmed inte behöver utföras av medicinsk personal. Ytterligare en fördel är att de regelbundna kontakterna med personerna är korta vilket möjliggör uppföljningar av en bred population. Detta gör BCIs till en kostnadseffektiv insats som kan erbjudas många personer och riskgrupper. I flera vetenskapliga studier som utvärderat BCI-insatser har man funnit positiva effekter i form av färre självmordsförsök och självmord (för systematiska översikter se: Zalsman et al., 2016; Mann et al 2022). Den upphandlade leverantören ska utveckla ett system som kan ta emot deltagare med förhöjd självmordsrisk. Systemet ska möjliggöra processer för att regelbundet följa upp dessa personer genom strukturerade telefonkontakter enligt våra riktlinjer som har syfte att förmedla medmänskligt stöd. Vid varje kontakttillfälle ska uppringaren kunna föra anteckningar som ska användas som underlag till nästa samtal. Samtliga delar av systemet ska vara utvecklade med de säkerhetsegenskaper som krävs för att kunna hantera känsliga personuppgifter enligt dataskyddsförordningen. För detta ändamål, se bifogat PUB-avtal som ska kunna signeras för att KI ska kunna ingå avtal med en leverantör angående detta projekt. Tjänsten kommer att vända sig till individer över 18 år. Den upphandlade leverantören ska kunna leverera tjänsten till så många personer som möjligt fram till år 2029, där varje person följs upp cirka åtta (8) gånger per år och varje kontakttillfälle tar ungefär 20 minuter. Vid utebliven kontakt ska den upphandlade leverantören följa studieprotokollets rutiner för upprepade kontaktförsök vid missat kontakttillfälle. Leverantören ska även kunna erbjuda personer möjligheten att specificera när på dagen de önskar bli kontaktade. Uppringare behöver inte ha formell klinisk utbildning men de ska ha relevant utbildning eller erfarenhet av att erbjuda socialt stöd (se krav nedan). NASP kommer i samband med projektet att bistå med utbildning omfattande cirka en heldag.
